description: Auto Drive backend and files-gateway health from the series they push to VictoriaMetrics. All series are events or periodic readings, not counters: queries count or sum over a window and never use rate().

panels.description: API and S3 requests in the selected range. One sample per API or S3 request, recorded after the handler returns. Handlers that throw go to the error middleware unrecorded, so errors are undercounted. Needs VICTORIA_ACTIVE=true on the backend.
panels.title: Requests

panels.description: Share of recorded requests that returned 5xx. One sample per API or S3 request, recorded after the handler returns. Handlers that throw go to the error middleware unrecorded, so errors are undercounted. Needs VICTORIA_ACTIVE=true on the backend.
panels.title: Server-error share

panels.description: Bytes in finalized uploads over the selected range.
panels.title: Uploaded

panels.description: Download bytes count only downloads charged to an account (requested byte range); anonymous downloads are not recorded.
panels.title: Downloaded, charged

panels.description: Highest number of queries queued for a Postgres connection in any backend process. Above 0 means a pool was exhausted.
panels.title: Peak Postgres pool waiters

panels.description: Worst 10 s p99 event-loop delay across backend processes.
panels.title: Worst event-loop delay p99

panels.description: Uploads parked as FAILED because their migration cannot succeed. Emitted only when it happens, so it shows 0 when the backends reported in the range and none was parked, and No data when no backend heartbeat arrived.
panels.title: Unrecoverable uploads

panels.description: files-gateway DSN object fetches that ended in an error (not success, not dropped). Shows 0 when fetches were recorded and none failed, and No data when the gateway sends no object_fetch metrics.
panels.title: Failed DSN fetches

panels.description: Requests per interval, by HTTP status. One sample per API or S3 request, recorded after the handler returns. Handlers that throw go to the error middleware unrecorded, so errors are undercounted. Needs VICTORIA_ACTIVE=true on the backend.
panels.title: Requests by status code

panels.description: Requests per interval, by how the caller authenticated. One sample per API or S3 request, recorded after the handler returns. Handlers that throw go to the error middleware unrecorded, so errors are undercounted. Needs VICTORIA_ACTIVE=true on the backend.
panels.title: Requests by auth provider

panels.description: Top 15 routes by request count over the selected range. Paths are Express route patterns without the router's mount prefix, so routers that share a pattern share a row: GET /:cid and GET /:cid/status cover both /objects and /downloads, and GET / covers /features and S3 ListBuckets. Known gaps lists the fix.
panels.title: Busiest routes

panels.description: Recorded 4xx and 5xx responses per route over the selected range. One sample per API or S3 request, recorded after the handler returns. Handlers that throw go to the error middleware unrecorded, so errors are undercounted. Needs VICTORIA_ACTIVE=true on the backend. Paths are Express route patterns without the router's mount prefix, so routers that share a pattern share a row: GET /:cid and GET /:cid/status cover both /objects and /downloads, and GET / covers /features and S3 ListBuckets. Known gaps lists the fix.
panels.title: Routes returning 4xx or 5xx

panels.description: Queries queued for a Postgres connection. Above 0 means the process's pool is exhausted. No host label: instances of the same process on different hosts merge into one series.
panels.title: Postgres pool clients waiting

panels.description: Most pool clients checked out (total minus idle) at the 10 s steps of a subquery over the interval. The red line is PG_POOL_MAX at its default of 10. No host label: instances of the same process on different hosts merge into one series, and each step reads only the sample written last. Instances keep a steady phase, so the same instance is read at every step and the others never show. The subquery errors on ranges longer than about 115 days. Known gaps lists the fix.
panels.title: Postgres pool clients in use

panels.description: Event-loop delay per 10 s window, net of the 10 ms sampling resolution. Dashed lines are max. No host label: instances of the same process on different hosts merge into one series.
panels.title: Event-loop delay p99 and max

panels.description: Each running instance reports 6 times a minute, so this estimates instances per process from the last minute of each interval. 0 means a process that reported in the previous 6 hours has stopped, or its samples are not arriving.

targets.expr:
sum by (process) (count_over_time(auto_drive_runtime_pg_pool_total{chain=~"(chain=)?$chain", process=~"$process"}[1m])) / 6
  or max by (process) (last_over_time(auto_drive_runtime_pg_pool_total{chain=~"(chain=)?$chain", process=~"$process"}[6h])) * 0

panels.title: Live instances per process

panels.description: Bytes per interval. Upload = finalized upload size. Download bytes count only downloads charged to an account (requested byte range); anonymous downloads are not recorded.
panels.title: Bytes by type

panels.description: Finalized uploads and charged downloads per interval. Download bytes count only downloads charged to an account (requested byte range); anonymous downloads are not recorded.
panels.title: Operations by type

panels.description: Mean bytes per operation in each interval. Download bytes count only downloads charged to an account (requested byte range); anonymous downloads are not recorded.
panels.title: Average size by type

panels.description: Bytes served per interval by the files-gateway, split by whether the file came from the DSN gateway. Recorded only for responses with a Content-Length header; chunked responses are skipped, so treat this as a sample of throughput, not a total. The gateway marks only file downloads with their origin, so "cache and other responses" also counts metadata JSON and the health and node endpoints.
panels.title: Bytes served by origin

panels.description: Total bytes divided by total response time in each interval. Recorded only for responses with a Content-Length header; chunked responses are skipped, so treat this as a sample of throughput, not a total. The gateway marks only file downloads with their origin, so "cache and other responses" also counts metadata JSON and the health and node endpoints.
panels.title: Transfer speed by origin

panels.description: p95 time from request to response finished. Recorded only for responses with a Content-Length header; chunked responses are skipped, so treat this as a sample of throughput, not a total. The gateway marks only file downloads with their origin, so "cache and other responses" also counts metadata JSON and the health and node endpoints.
panels.title: Response time p95 by origin

panels.description: DSN object fetches per interval by outcome. Empty if the live files-gateway predates the fetch metrics (gateway main, 2026-10-28). Failure outcomes are shades of red.
panels.title: Fetches by outcome

panels.description: Successful fetches only, worst gateway. High queue time with normal in-flight time means the retriever is saturated; high in-flight time means a slow gateway.
panels.title: Fetch time p95: total, waiting for a slot, in flight

panels.description: Fetches that used more than one attempt (max 3).
panels.title: Fetches that needed a retry

panels.description: Fetches that ended in an error (not success, not dropped) over the selected range, the same set as Failed DSN fetches. gateway is the index of the configured gateway URL.
panels.title: Failures by gateway and outcome
DAG indexer fallback (pinned fallback branch only)

panels.description: DAG indexer misses the gateway answered from the DSN, counted per lookup, not per download. failed = a rebuild failed, and the request with it; chunk_list_incomplete = the indexer is dropping nodes, and is usually followed by chunk_list_rebuilt or failed for the same file. Lookups served from already rebuilt chunk lists are in the next panel. Only the files-gateway fallback branch that Auto Drive pins sends this metric.
panels.title: Fallbacks by outcome

panels.description: Lookups answered from the gateway's in-memory cache of chunk lists rebuilt from the DSN. They cost no DSN traffic, but each one is a request for a file the indexer is missing. Counted per lookup: the gateway looks the list up for every chunk or byte-range request, and again when it checks compression and copies the file to its file cache, so one download can add thousands.
panels.title: Rebuilt chunk lists served from cache

panels.description: Compare with DAG_INDEXER_FALLBACK_MAX_NODES: values near it mean rebuilds are hitting the limit.
panels.title: Nodes walked per rebuild, p95

panels.description: Links the DAG indexer had not indexed, found while rebuilding.
panels.title: Unindexed links found

panels.description: Uploads set to FAILED because their migration cannot succeed. Any bar needs a look. Emitted only when it happens, so intervals with a backend heartbeat and no event show 0, and intervals without a heartbeat stay empty.
panels.title: Uploads parked as unrecoverable

panels.description: Objects reported by users per interval. Intervals with a backend heartbeat and no report show 0, and intervals without a heartbeat stay empty.
panels.title: Objects reported by users

panels.description: The poller writes every 5 minutes by default (USDC_TREASURY_BALANCE_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS). A series that stops means the poller stopped; balance is omitted when it cannot be read.
panels.title: Balance against cap

panels.description: Cap minus balance from the latest poll. Omitted when the balance cannot be read.
panels.title: Headroom before auto-pause

panels.description: 1 = true. Only environments where USDC gates run report these.
panels.title: Paused and stale

options.content:
These panels stay empty until Auto Drive sends more. Nothing in infra can fill them.

| Missing | Effect here | Smallest Auto Drive change |
|---|---|---|
| Request duration | No API latency panel | Add `duration_ms` to `auto_drive_api_request`, and record requests whose handler throws |
| Mount prefix on route paths | Busiest routes and the 4xx/5xx table merge `/objects/:cid` with `/downloads/:cid` (and their `/status` routes), and `/features` with S3 ListBuckets as `GET /` | Record `req.baseUrl + req.route.path` as `path` |
| Upload, completion and migration timings | Upload performance is bytes only | Duration fields when an upload finalizes and when a migration task ends |
| Publish-worker metrics | Publishing throughput and confirmation lag only from the queue and Postgres | Batch size, batch duration and confirmation lag from the publish worker |
| Cache tier and latency in the backend download API | Backend download serving is invisible; only the gateway side shows | Tier label (memory, filesystem, DSN) and duration per download |
| Host label | Instances of one process merge into one series | Add a hostname tag to every metric |
| Pool clients in use per sample | Pool clients in use reads one instance per 10 s step through a subquery, and errors on ranges longer than about 115 days | Send `pg_pool_in_use` (total minus idle) in the runtime heartbeat |
| Parsed `METRIC_ENVIRONMENT_TAG` | Every query needs the `(chain=)?` regex | Parse the tag before sending |
| Origin on every files-gateway response | No cache hit share, and the cache series also counts metadata, health and node responses | Set `x-file-origin` on every response, or track bandwidth on the file route only |
| Anonymous downloads | Download volume undercounts public traffic | Emit `auto_drive_interactions_size` for anonymous downloads too |

Queue depth, active jobs, the publishing backlog and host load need a CloudWatch or PostgreSQL datasource; they are follow-ups in infra, not app changes.
